title: Tensor, unit and coefficient compatibility of the finite evaluation equivalence.
statement:
/-- Tensor, unit and coefficient compatibility of the finite evaluation equivalence.
Source: blueprint `cor-galois-lisse-representations`, proof steps 3-5;
Stacks Project, Tag 0DV5 (3).

Exact Lean statement:
theorem galois_lisse_finite_compatibility
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (y : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y) (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
    [∀ P, MulAction G ((FiniteEtale.fiber y).obj P)]
    (d : GaloisLisseFiniteData y G) (h : galoisFiniteEvaluationAction y G d) :
    galoisFiniteUnit y G d ∧ galoisFiniteTensor y G d ∧
      galoisFiniteScalarExtension y G d

proof.text:
*(1): naturality of the action.* By [def-galois-fibre-functor] an element $\sigma\in\pi_1$ is a natural automorphism of $F_{\bar y}$ on $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$, so for every map $\phi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ of finite locally constant sheaves of sets, $\phi_{\bar y}\circ\sigma_{\mathcal A}=\sigma_{\mathcal B}\circ\phi_{\bar y}$. The product $\mathcal A\times\mathcal B$ lies in $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ (on a common trivializing covering $\underline S\times\underline T=\underline{S\times T}$) and $(\mathcal A\times\mathcal B)_{\bar y}=\mathcal A_{\bar y}\times\mathcal B_{\bar y}$ through the two projections; applying naturality to the two projections shows that $\sigma$ acts on $(\mathcal A\times\mathcal B)_{\bar y}$ diagonally. Formalization subproblem: put the sheaf tensor product and constant unit on the lisse subcategory.
The stalk tensor comparison is equivariant: apply naturality of gamma to the
bilinear map of underlying finite locally constant sheaves; it sends pure
tensors to the diagonal action. This lifts the canonical braided constraints.
Every element of a constant stalk is the germ of a constant global section;
naturality with its map from the terminal sheaf shows that gamma fixes it.
This proves the unit statement also for noncommutative finite rings.
Restrict sheafified balanced scalar extension to lisse objects. For a coefficient
b, naturality of gamma for z mapped to b tensor z makes its stalk comparison
equivariant. Lift this comparison through the fully faithful equivalence.
For composites, use the sheaf and module scalar-extension associators; both paths
on pure germs send b tensor (a tensor z) to b*g(a) tensor z. These generate
after sheafification, and equivalence faithfulness proves the compatibility.

*(1): tensor products and the unit.* Let $\Lambda$ be commutative and $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ locally constant of finite $\Lambda$-modules. By [lem-pod-lisse-tensor-and-scalar-extension] (2), $\mathcal F\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G$ is locally constant of finite $\Lambda$-modules and $c:\mathcal F_{\bar y}\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G_{\bar y}\to(\mathcal F\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G)_{\bar y}$, $s_{\bar y}\otimes t_{\bar y}\mapsto(s\otimes t)_{\bar y}$, is an isomorphism, natural and compatible with the associativity, commutativity and unit constraints. The canonical bilinear map $\beta:\mathcal F\times\mathcal G\to\mathcal F\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G$ is a map of finite locally constant sheaves of sets, and its stalk is $(a,b)\mapsto c(a\otimes b)$; by step 3, $\beta_{\bar y}\circ(\sigma\times\sigma)=\sigma\circ\beta_{\bar y}$, i.e. $\sigma(c(a\otimes b))=c(\sigma a\otimes\sigma b)$. Since the $a\otimes b$ generate $\mathcal F_{\bar y}\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G_{\bar y}$ additively and $\sigma$ is additive, $c$ is $\pi_1$-equivariant for the diagonal action on the source. For the unit: by [lem-pod-lisse-tensor-and-scalar-extension] (1) every element of $(\underline\Lambda)_{\bar y}=\Lambda$ is the germ of a global constant section $x$, i.e. the image of the point under the stalk of the map $x:\underline{\{*\}}\to\underline\Lambda$; naturality (step 3) for this map, with $\sigma$ the identity on the one-point stalk, gives $\sigma(x_{\bar y})=x_{\bar y}$, so $\underline\Lambda$ goes to the trivial representation $\Lambda$. Formalization subproblem: put the sheaf tensor product and constant unit on the lisse subcategory.
The stalk tensor comparison is equivariant: apply naturality of gamma to the
bilinear map of underlying finite locally constant sheaves; it sends pure
tensors to the diagonal action. This lifts the canonical braided constraints.
Every element of a constant stalk is the germ of a constant global section;
naturality with its map from the terminal sheaf shows that gamma fixes it.
This proves the unit statement also for noncommutative finite rings.
Restrict sheafified balanced scalar extension to lisse objects. For a coefficient
b, naturality of gamma for z mapped to b tensor z makes its stalk comparison
equivariant. Lift this comparison through the fully faithful equivalence.
For composites, use the sheaf and module scalar-extension associators; both paths
on pure germs send b tensor (a tensor z) to b*g(a) tensor z. These generate
after sheafification, and equivalence faithfulness proves the compatibility.

*(1): base change of coefficients.* Let $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a homomorphism of finite rings. By [lem-pod-lisse-tensor-and-scalar-extension] (3), $\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F$ is locally constant of finite $\Lambda'$-modules and $\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F_{\bar y}\to(\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F)_{\bar y}$, $\lambda'\otimes s_{\bar y}\mapsto(\lambda'\otimes s)_{\bar y}$, is an isomorphism, natural in $\mathcal F$ and compatible with composites. For each $\lambda'\in\Lambda'$, the map $\mathcal F\to\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F$, $s\mapsto\lambda'\otimes s$, is a map of finite locally constant sheaves of sets, so by step 3 its stalk commutes with every $\sigma$: $\sigma(\lambda'\otimes m)=\lambda'\otimes\sigma m$ for $m\in\mathcal F_{\bar y}$. These elements generate $\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F_{\bar y}$ additively, so the isomorphism is $\pi_1$-equivariant for the action $1\otimes\sigma$, which proves the compatibility with base change. Formalization subproblem: put the sheaf tensor product and constant unit on the lisse subcategory.
The stalk tensor comparison is equivariant: apply naturality of gamma to the
bilinear map of underlying finite locally constant sheaves; it sends pure
tensors to the diagonal action. This lifts the canonical braided constraints.
Every element of a constant stalk is the germ of a constant global section;
naturality with its map from the terminal sheaf shows that gamma fixes it.
This proves the unit statement also for noncommutative finite rings.

after sheafification, and equivalence faithfulness proves the compatibility.

mathlib_searches.query: An equivalence between finite locally constant module sheaves and finite continuous representations, compatible with stalks and tensor products
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits, primarily Mathlib.Condensed.Discrete.Module; no scheme-etale or adic correspondence. Earlier fundamental-group query found the abstract functorToContAction equivalence only.

mathlib_searches.query: Integral adic sheaves and continuous finite dimensional p-adic representations, tensor products and scalar extension
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits on AdicCompletion, including ofTensorProductEquivOfFiniteNoetherian, but no sheaf-representation equivalence or monoidal comparison.
mathlib_searches.verdict: Useful finite-module infrastructure already covered by the declared adic-limit dependency; no exact match.

mathlib_searches.results: LocalSystems proves the finite commutative-ring equivalence; it does not cover all noncommutative finite rings nor the adic clauses. EquivalenceInternalModule proves transport of internal modules, and its finite-action identification is stated. No adic-category equivalence was found.
mathlib_searches.verdict: Reuse the declared modules for the parts they cover; the missing comparison/glue is stated here.
